## Beyond decibels

How does a city sound, and how differently do we experience it? [**HearHere**](https://www.citizenscience.uzh.ch/en/projects/hearhere.html) brings citizens and researchers together to explore Zurich's everyday soundscapes. Rather than relying on noise levels alone, the project captures how urban sound actually feels to the people moving through it.

Using a mobile sensing app, participants contribute short ambient audio recordings, GPS locations, and subjective ratings of their experiences. These contributions will help build a community-driven, multidimensional noise map that identifies both **noise hotspots** and **acoustic relief zones**.

## Diverse experiences, shared knowledge

HearHere welcomes anyone living in or visiting Zurich, including people with hearing loss, hearing aids, tinnitus, hyperacusis, or neurodivergent sensory experiences. No prior knowledge is required.

Alongside mobile data collection, participants can contribute to workshops with scientists and policymakers to interpret findings and co-create recommendations for more inclusive urban planning.

## From pilot to broader participation

According to the project overview, the initial pilot involved more than 20 participants and over 100 geospatial audio measurements across Zurich. The next stages focus on broader participation, continued data collection, and developing an interactive map and resources for the public.

Visit the [HearHere page at Citizen Science Zurich](https://www.citizenscience.uzh.ch/en/projects/hearhere.html) for the project phases and information about participating, or explore HearHere alongside our [ongoing research projects](../../projects.qmd#hearhere).
